Title: Antenatal magnesium sulphate for the prevention of cerebral palsy in infants born preterm: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, multi-centre trial
Author: Wolf et al.
Comment: Table 2 explicitly reports arm headers of 343 magnesium-exposed and 337 placebo-exposed fetuses/children and percentages consistent with those denominators (12/343 and 19/337); these randomised child-level denominators were therefore extracted. Figure 1 separately states that 321 and 313 children survived to follow-up and were followed through medical records, but Table 2 does not present the cerebral-palsy event counts using those survivor denominators. The paper reports an adjusted odds ratio, not a risk ratio; the review can calculate an unadjusted risk ratio from the extracted events and totals. Adjusted analyses accounted for twin correlation using generalized estimating equations and adjusted for plurality and gestational age.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Antenatal magnesium sulphate') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicentre trial
Publication Status: Accepted manuscript; peer reviewed but not yet copyedited, typeset, paginated, or proofread
domain: Fetal neuroprotection in threatened preterm birth
Content length: Loading dose of 5 grams infused over 20 to 30 minutes, followed by 1 gram per hour until delivery or for 24 hours; one repeat loading dose permitted
Topic of Content: Antenatal magnesium sulphate for prevention of cerebral palsy in children born preterm
Participant type: Children born to randomised pregnant women at risk of delivery before 32 weeks; singleton and twin pregnancies included
Outcome measurement: Any cerebral palsy diagnosis at a minimum corrected age of 18 months. Medical records were scrutinized by HTW for CP diagnosis and GMFCS level; routine follow-up was by a neonatologist experienced in preterm follow-up or a paediatric neurologist for children born before 32 weeks, while suspected neurological disability in later-born children prompted paediatric referral. ASQ responses corroborated records, and an independent neuro-paediatrician examined children when indicated.

Author: Caroline A. Crowther et al.
Comment: Used the cerebral-palsy-specific denominators (children with cerebral palsy data), not randomized infants and not the death-or-cerebral-palsy composite denominators. The reported adjusted RR was adjusted for hospital site, gestational age at entry, and plurality. Design Type: Multicenter, blinded, parallel-group, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
domain: Antenatal fetal neuroprotection and child neurodevelopment
Topic of Content: Antenatal magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection before expected preterm birth at 30 to 34 weeks’ gestation

Title: Effect of Magnesium Sulfate Given for Neuroprotection Before Preterm Birth: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Crowther et al.
Comment: Outcome-specific denominators are children with cerebral-palsy data (533 magnesium, 513 placebo), not the Table 2 header totals of infants alive at randomization. Fourteen children lacking cerebral-palsy assessments were excluded (9 magnesium, 5 placebo). Counts are child-level. Title: Association between the use of antenatal magnesium sulfate in preterm labor and adverse health outcomes in infants
Author: Mittendorf et al.
Comment: The paper does not report an outcome-specific denominator for surviving children assessed for cerebral palsy at 18 months. Therefore, the explicitly reported infant arm totals (30 MgSO4 and 29 saline placebo) were used as the only available denominators; these are infants born/randomized to each arm, not confirmed numbers with cerebral-palsy follow-up data. There were two deaths in the MgSO4 arm and one in the saline arm. Each arm included one twin pair, randomization was maternal, and no clustering adjustment is stated. The 3 MgSO4 events are directly obtained from one infant with PVL and cerebral palsy plus two infants with cerebral palsy only; placebo had no cerebral-palsy cases. No cerebral-palsy-specific P value or risk ratio was reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('4-g intravenous MgSO4 bolus') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Antenatal fetal neuroprotection / cerebral palsy prevention in preterm birth
Study Environment: Hospital-based trial with special follow-up clinic visits
Topic of Content: Antenatal magnesium sulfate for prevention of cerebral injury in threatened preterm birth
interaction_type: Maternal intravenous treatment with child neurodevelopmental follow-up
Participant type: Children born to women in preterm labor at >24 and <34 completed weeks of gestation
Recruitment source: Women admitted to hospital in preterm labor, with or without premature rupture of membranes
Outcome measurement: Cerebral palsy among surviving children; follow-up examinations occurred at 4, 8, 12, and 18 corrected months, and diagnoses were made or verified by a developmental pediatrician after the 18-month examination. The paper does not state a more specific diagnostic criterion.
effect_direction: Favours placebo (more cerebral palsy events with magnesium)

Title: A Randomized, Controlled Trial of Magnesium Sulfate for the Prevention of Cerebral Palsy
Author: Rouse et al.
Comment: The paper reports child-level cerebral-palsy events (41 and 74) but gives pregnancy-level denominators (942 and 1002 pregnancies), with 40 and 73 affected pregnancies. Because the synthesis contract requires children as both events and totals, the pregnancy denominators were not entered as child totals and no RR was calculated. The analysis unit for primary outcomes/components was the pregnancy; twin pregnancies could contain more than one affected child. Ninety-five percent of cerebral-palsy examinations were completed by 32 months corrected age, and three diagnoses were based on the 1-year examination.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Magnesium sulfate') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
domain: Antenatal fetal neuroprotection and cerebral palsy prevention
Study Environment: 20 participating NICHD Maternal–Fetal Medicine Units Network sites
Topic of Content: Magnesium sulfate for prevention of cerebral palsy after threatened early preterm birth
Participant type: Children born to randomized women at imminent risk of delivery between 24 and 31 weeks of gestation
Recruitment source: 20 participating NICHD Maternal–Fetal Medicine Units Network sites
Outcome measurement: Cerebral palsy diagnosed by an annually certified pediatrician or pediatric neurologist when at least two of three features were present: gross-motor milestone delay of 30% or more; specified abnormalities of tone, deep-tendon reflexes, or movement; or persistence of primitive reflexes/absence of protective reflexes. Severity was classified using the GMFCS. The goal was diagnosis at the 2-year corrected-age examination; specified children could be declared free at 1 year, and unresolved cases could be adjudicated from the 1-year examination.
